kartik: hypothesis: when prefix KV is stored as fp16 vs int8-quantized we change the estimated working set, which affects kernel scoring. if quantized-kv reduces footprint we should prefer fused kernel again.

maria: but forcing fused increases transient memory pressure when cache is bf16; we saw OOMs on a few shards earlier. need safe guard.
kartik: maybe add a lightweight pre-check: if estimated_free_mem_after_alloc > fused_extra_mem_margin && estimated_kv_bytes < kv_quant_threshold then prefer fused. smaller change than full routing rewrite.

devin: another angle: batcher heuristics. we saw many tail requests with long prefixes get coalesced into batches that trigger generic kernel due to mixed seq lengths. if we tighten adaptive batcher by grouping on prefix_len_bucket we can keep fused on the hot path.
maria: quick config to try: set batcher.group_by = [model, prefix_bucket(<=512, <=1024, >1024)], batcher.max_mix_ratio=0.2. also lower cross-batch shape smoothing lambda.
kartik: also consider prefix-aware prefetch: pre-populate KV cache quantized (int8) for prefixes at request start so memory estimate used by router is accurate. this will affect cache eviction policy (LRU -> size-aware).
